## Behaviour changes

- **Sites now see who is fetching.** The fetch tool, `Fetch` in `cn`, `@url` and the favicon lookup send `User-Agent: Continuous-User/<major>.<minor> (+https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/blob/main/docs/web-agent.md)` instead of `node-fetch`; the docs crawler sends `Continuous-Crawler/<major>.<minor> (+…)` instead of `node-fetch` (Cheerio) or a Chrome 88 string (Chromium); `@web`, `search_web` and `@google` send `Continuous-User/<major>.<minor>` alone. The string carries no operating system, editor, patch version or id. Pages read for you ask for Markdown first (`Accept: text/markdown, text/html;q=0.9, …`). A site that blocked `node-fetch` may now let the request through, and one that blocks unknown agents may refuse it: `web.userAgent` in your own config.yaml chooses `generic-agent`, a browser preset or a custom string, and `web.hosts.<pattern>.userAgent` does it for some hosts only. `robots.txt` is checked as `Continuous-User` whatever you choose. A project or assistant config cannot change any of this.
- `web.acceptLanguage`, `web.hosts.<pattern>.headers` and `web.limits.maxRedirects` are now in force. A per-host header goes only to hosts that match the pattern and not to a redirect elsewhere; `maxRedirects` (default 5, ceiling 10) applies to every path on the guarded fetch, and a project or assistant config may only lower it.
